# Part 1: The Question

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## The Traditional Question {background-color="#f8f9fa"}

::: {style="text-align: center; font-size: 2em; margin-top: .5em;"}
"Which **factors** predict success?"
:::

::: {style="text-align: center; color: #666; margin-top: .5em;"}
*Regression logic: each factor in isolation*
:::

::: {.fragment style="margin-top: 2em; padding: 1em; background: #fff3cd; border-radius: 8px; text-align: center;"}
**Problem:** Assumes factors work independently — but in reality, success depends on *combinations*
:::

## The Configurational Question {background-color="#1e3a5f"}

:::::: {style="color: white;"}
::: {style="text-align: center; font-size: 2em; margin-top: .5em;"}
"What **combinations** of factors lead to success?"
:::

::: {style="text-align: center; opacity: 0.9; margin-top: 1em;"}
*QCA logic: configurations, not individual effects*
:::

::: {.fragment style="margin-top: 2em; padding: 1em; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.15); border-radius: 8px; text-align: center;"}
**Key insight:** Multiple pathways can lead to the same outcome (equifinality)
:::
::::::

::: notes
-   Traditional evaluation asks "What predicts success?" — each factor in isolation.
-   We ask "What combinations of factors reliably lead to success?" — that's configurationalism.
:::

## What We Want to Know

::: r-fit-text
Which programme features lead to **sucess**?
:::

. . .

But "success" means different things:

| Outcome | What it measures | How common in FCDO reports? |
|----|----|----|
| Exceptional Performance | A++/A+ overall rating | Rare (16%) |
| Impact Achievement | Achieved intended impact | Common (80%) |
| Sustainability | Benefits will continue | Common (69%) |
| Equity Outcomes | Reached marginalized groups | Moderate (34%) |

# Part 3: The Method

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## What is QCA?

**Qualitative Comparative Analysis** asks:

> "What combinations of conditions are associated with an outcome?"


::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
### Traditional regression

-   Effect of X on Y, controlling for Z
-   Assumes variables work independently
-   "On average, funding flexibility increases impact by 0.3 points"
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### QCA approach

-   What combinations lead to success?
-   Conditions work together
-   "Funding flexibility + local embedding + GESI focus → equity outcomes"
:::
:::::

## The Key Question {background-color="#f8f9fa"}

```{=html}
<div style="text-align: center; margin-bottom: 0.3em;">
<h3 style="color: #1e3a5f; margin: 0; font-size: 1.1em;">Which conditions matter for success?</h3>
</div>

<div style="display: flex; justify-content: center; gap: 1.5em; align-items: flex-start;">

<!-- Necessary Venn: Success is SUBSET of Condition -->
<div style="text-align: center;">
<svg width="240" height="180" viewBox="0 0 240 180">
  <!-- Outer circle: Condition -->
  <circle cx="120" cy="90" r="80" fill="#bbdefb" stroke="#1976d2" stroke-width="3"/>
  <!-- Inner circle: Success (inside condition) -->
  <circle cx="120" cy="105" r="42" fill="#1976d2"/>
  <!-- Labels -->
  <text x="120" y="35" text-anchor="middle" fill="#1976d2" font-weight="bold" font-size="12">Condition</text>
  <text x="120" y="110" text-anchor="middle" fill="white" font-weight="bold" font-size="12">Success</text>
</svg>
<div style="font-size: 1em; font-weight: bold; color: #1976d2;">NECESSARY</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.7em; color: #777;"><em>"Can't succeed without it"</em></div>
</div>

<!-- Sufficient Venn: Condition is SUBSET of Success -->
<div style="text-align: center;">
<svg width="240" height="180" viewBox="0 0 240 180">
  <!-- Outer circle: Success -->
  <circle cx="120" cy="90" r="80" fill="#c8e6c9" stroke="#388e3c" stroke-width="3"/>
  <!-- Inner circle: Condition (inside success) -->
  <circle cx="120" cy="105" r="42" fill="#388e3c"/>
  <!-- Labels -->
  <text x="120" y="35" text-anchor="middle" fill="#388e3c" font-weight="bold" font-size="12">Success</text>
  <text x="120" y="110" text-anchor="middle" fill="white" font-weight="bold" font-size="12">Condition</text>
</svg>
<div style="font-size: 1em; font-weight: bold; color: #388e3c;">SUFFICIENT</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.7em; color: #777;"><em>"If present, always succeeds"</em></div>
</div>

<!-- Both: Overlapping Venn -->
<div style="text-align: center;">
<svg width="240" height="180" viewBox="0 0 240 180">
  <!-- Circle A: Condition -->
  <circle cx="85" cy="90" r="65" fill="#bbdefb" fill-opacity="0.7" stroke="#1976d2" stroke-width="3"/>
  <!-- Circle B: Success -->
  <circle cx="155" cy="90" r="65" fill="#c8e6c9" fill-opacity="0.7" stroke="#388e3c" stroke-width="3"/>
  <!-- Labels -->
  <text x="45" y="95" text-anchor="middle" fill="#1976d2" font-weight="bold" font-size="11">Condition</text>
  <text x="195" y="95" text-anchor="middle" fill="#388e3c" font-weight="bold" font-size="11">Success</text>
  <text x="120" y="95" text-anchor="middle" fill="#333" font-weight="bold" font-size="11">Both</text>
</svg>
<div style="font-size: 1em; font-weight: bold; color: #f57c00;">QCA FINDS</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.7em; color: #777;"><em>Both types</em></div>
</div>

</div>
```

::: {.fragment style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.3em; padding: 0.5em; background: #fff3e0; border-radius: 10px; border-left: 4px solid #f57c00; font-size: 0.9em;"}
**QCA finds both:** *necessary* (must-haves) AND *sufficient* (guarantees success)
:::

## Two Types of Relationships

::::::: columns
:::: {.column width="50%"}
### Necessary Conditions

**Must be present** for the outcome to occur

::: callout-note
## Example

"You need a passport to travel internationally"

No passport → Cannot travel Having passport → Doesn't guarantee travel
:::

**Test**: Of all successful cases, how many have this condition?
::::

:::: {.column width="50%"}
### Sufficient Conditions

**Guarantee** the outcome when present

::: callout-tip
## Example

"A winning lottery ticket guarantees money"

Winning ticket → Definitely get money No ticket → Could still get money other ways
:::

**Test**: Of all cases with this condition, how many succeed?
::::
:::::::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## The Key Insight: Prevalence Shapes Our Analysis

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
### When outcomes are RARE (16%)

**Necessity analysis is informative**

-   If 100% of successes have a feature, that's meaningful
-   Finding "recipes" is hard (few successful cases)

*Example: Exceptional Performance*
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### When outcomes are COMMON (80%)

**Sufficiency analysis is informative**

-   Many conditions will seem "necessary" by chance
-   Finding reliable "recipes" is easier

*Example: Impact Achievement*
:::
:::::

::: callout-note
## Why this matters

We use **different analytical strategies** for different outcomes based on how common they are.

*See: Schneider & Wagemann (2012) on "trivialness"; Braumoeller & Goertz (2000) on necessary conditions methodology*
:::

## Understanding QCA Metrics {background-color="#f0f4f8"}

```{=html}
<div style="display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 0.8em; margin-top: 0.3em;">

<div style="background: #e8f5e9; padding: 0.6em; border-radius: 8px; border-left: 4px solid #388e3c;">
<div style="font-weight: bold; color: #388e3c; font-size: 0.8em; margin-bottom: 0.2em;">🎯 Necessity Consistency</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.55em; color: #333; line-height: 1.4;">
<strong>Question:** When outcome is present, is the condition also present?
<br><strong>Threshold:** ≥0.90 (condition in 90%+ of successful cases)
<br><em style="color: #666;">High = condition is a "must-have"</em>
</div>
</div>

<div style="background: #e3f2fd; padding: 0.6em; border-radius: 8px; border-left: 4px solid #1976d2;">
<div style="font-weight: bold; color: #1976d2; font-size: 0.8em; margin-bottom: 0.2em;">📏 Sufficiency Consistency (incl.cut)</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.55em; color: #333; line-height: 1.4;">
<strong>Question:** When condition pattern is present, does outcome follow?
<br><strong>Our threshold:** incl.cut = 0.85 (85% of cases succeed)
<br><em style="color: #666;">High = pathway reliably produces success</em>
</div>
</div>

<div style="background: #fce4ec; padding: 0.6em; border-radius: 8px; border-left: 4px solid #c2185b;">
<div style="font-weight: bold; color: #c2185b; font-size: 0.8em; margin-bottom: 0.2em;">📊 Coverage</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.55em; color: #333; line-height: 1.4;">
<strong>Question:** What % of successful cases does this pathway explain?
<br><strong>Our solutions:** 65-75% coverage (3 valid outcomes)
<br><em style="color: #666;">High = pathways capture most routes to success</em>
</div>
</div>

<div style="background: #fff3e0; padding: 0.6em; border-radius: 8px; border-left: 4px solid #f57c00;">
<div style="font-weight: bold; color: #f57c00; font-size: 0.8em; margin-bottom: 0.2em;">🔢 Frequency Threshold</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.55em; color: #333; line-height: 1.4;">
<strong>Question:** Minimum cases to consider a pathway empirically grounded?
<br><strong>Our thresholds:** 2 (rare outcomes) or 3 (common outcomes)
<br><em style="color: #666;">Balances pattern detection with empirical support</em>
</div>
</div>

</div>
```

::: {.fragment style="margin-top: 0.3em; padding: 0.4em; background: #f5f5f5; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 0.6em; text-align: center;"}
**Key thresholds:** Necessity ≥0.90 \| Sufficiency (incl.cut) ≥0.85 \| n.cut = 2-3 depending on outcome prevalence
:::

## The Metrics Explained

### Consistency: "How reliable is this pattern?"

$$\text{Consistency} = \frac{\text{Cases with condition AND outcome}}{\text{Cases with condition}}$$

-   **0.85+ = Reliable** (85%+ of cases with this pattern succeed)
-   Below 0.85 = Too many exceptions to trust

### Coverage: "How much does this explain?"

$$\text{Coverage} = \frac{\text{Cases with condition AND outcome}}{\text{All successful cases}}$$

-   High coverage = This pattern explains many successes
-   Low coverage = This is just one of many routes to success

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## How to Read the ESA Results

### The 5 steps we report for each outcome:

| Step | What it does | What to look for |
|:---------------|:-----------------------|:-------------------------------|
| **Step 1: Necessity** | Tests if conditions are *prerequisites* | Consistency ≥90% means "almost always present when outcome occurs" |
| **Steps 2-3: Truth Table** | Maps all observed configurations | How many configs are sufficient vs. insufficient |
| **Step 5: SUIN Check** | Tests for INUS conditions | Does any condition appear in ALL pathways? |
| **Step 6: Parsimonious** | Identifies the "recipes" | Pathways that reliably produce the outcome |

## Outcome 2: Impact Achievement

::: callout-note
No INUS conditions identified. No single condition appears in all pathways as a necessary component.

**Step 6: Parsimonious Solution**[^2]

[^2]: 16 equivalent solutions exist; pathways 1-2 stable across all

```{r}
impact_paths <- data.frame(
  Pathway = c("OutputsAccessible", 
              "PartnershipEquity * ~EquityGESI",
              "~SharedGovernance * OutputsCapacity * ~FundingLongevity",
              "~SharedGovernance * ~LocalEmbedded * ImpactStrategy"),
  Interpretation = c("Accessible outputs alone", 
                     "Equitable partnerships, no GESI focus",
                     "Centralized + capacity + standard funding",
                     "Centralized + not embedded + impact strategy")
)
kable(impact_paths, format = "html", col.names = c("Pathway", "Interpretation")) %>%
  kable_styling(font_size = 18)
```

**Consistency: 0.881** ✓ \| **Coverage: 74.6%**

## Outcome 4: Equity Outcomes

### ESA Steps 5-6: SUIN Check & Parsimonious Solution

**Step 5: SUIN Check**

::: callout-important
## INUS Condition Found!

**EquityGESI appears in ALL 3 pathways** → INUS condition (Insufficient but Necessary part of Unnecessary but Sufficient configurations)
:::

**Step 6: Parsimonious Solution** *(Unique solution - no model ambiguity)*

```{r}
equity_paths <- data.frame(
  Pathway = c("SelectionProcedures * EquityGESI", 
              "~LocalEmbedded * EquityGESI",
              "OutputsAccessible * EquityGESI * InstabilityResponse"),
  Interpretation = c("Competitive selection + GESI", 
                     "Not locally embedded + GESI",
                     "Accessible + crisis adaptation + GESI")
)
kable(equity_paths, format = "html", col.names = c("Pathway", "Interpretation")) %>%
  kable_styling(font_size = 18)
```

**Consistency: 0.987** ✓ (highest!) \| **Coverage: 74.3%**

# Part 5: Putting It All Together

## Summary: Four Different Stories

```{r}
summary_df <- data.frame(
  Outcome = c("Exceptional\nPerformance", "Impact\nAchievement", "Sustainability", "Equity\nOutcomes"),
  Pattern = c("Prerequisites exist,\nbut no recipe works", 
              "4 different recipes,\n1 is very simple",
              "3 recipes,\ntime matters",
              "1 ingredient is\nnon-negotiable"),
  Key_Finding = c("3 necessary conditions\n(100%, 98%, 96%)",
                  "Accessible outputs\nalone is enough",
                  "Extended funding in\n2 of 3 recipes",
                  "GESI focus in\nALL 3 recipes")
)

kable(summary_df, format = "html", 
      col.names = c("Outcome", "The pattern", "Key finding")) %>%
  kable_styling(font_size = 24) %>%
  row_spec(1, background = "#fadbd8") %>%
  row_spec(2, background = "#d5f5e3") %>%
  row_spec(3, background = "#d6eaf8") %>%
  row_spec(4, background = "#e8daef")
```

## Visual Summary

```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 14

results_df <- data.frame(
  Outcome = rep(c("Exceptional", "Impact", "Sustainability", "Equity"), 2),
  Metric = c(rep("Consistency", 4), rep("Coverage", 4)),
  Value = c(0.286, 0.881, 0.870, 0.987, 0.082, 0.746, 0.648, 0.743),
  Pass = c("Fail", "Pass", "Pass", "Pass", "Fail", "Pass", "Pass", "Pass")
)

results_df$Outcome <- factor(results_df$Outcome, 
                              levels = c("Exceptional", "Impact", "Sustainability", "Equity"))

ggplot(results_df, aes(x = Outcome, y = Value, fill = Metric, alpha = Pass)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.85, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", linewidth = 1.5) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0.89, label = "Reliability threshold (0.85)", 
           color = "red", hjust = 0, size = 5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Consistency" = "#3498db", "Coverage" = "#e67e22")) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c("Fail" = 0.4, "Pass" = 1), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(), limits = c(0, 1.05)) +
  labs(y = "", x = "", fill = "") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 18) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

::: fragment
**Only Exceptional Performance fails** — we can find reliable recipes for the other three outcomes
:::

## Why Does Prevalence Matter?

```{r}
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 12

explanation_df <- data.frame(
  x = c(1, 2),
  y = c(1, 1),
  Prevalence = c("Low (16%)\nExceptional Performance", "High (80%)\nImpact Achievement"),
  Analysis = c("Necessity analysis\nis meaningful", "Sufficiency analysis\nis meaningful"),
  Why = c("Finding that 100% of successes\nhave a feature is informative\nwhen successes are rare", 
          "Finding reliable recipes\nis possible when\nmost programmes succeed")
)

ggplot(explanation_df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = Prevalence), width = 0.8, height = 0.6, alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_text(aes(label = Prevalence), vjust = -2, size = 6, fontface = "bold") +
  geom_text(aes(label = Analysis), vjust = 0, size = 5, color = "#2c3e50") +
  geom_text(aes(label = Why), vjust = 3, size = 4, color = "#7f8c8d") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Low (16%)\nExceptional Performance" = "#e74c3c",
                               "High (80%)\nImpact Achievement" = "#3498db")) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  xlim(0.3, 2.7) + ylim(-0.5, 2)
```

# Part 6: What Should FCDO Do?

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Recommendation 1: Mandate the Prerequisites

For **ALL programmes**, require:

:::::: columns
::: {.column width="33%"}
### ✅ Impact Strategy

Document clear, evidence-based impact pathways

*100% of exceptional programmes had this*
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
### ✅ M&E Systems

Strengthen monitoring and evaluation over time

*98% of exceptional programmes did this*
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
### ✅ Strategic Clarity

Articulate contribution to broader goals

*96% of exceptional programmes had this*
:::
::::::

. . .

::: callout-note
These won't guarantee excellence, but you almost certainly won't achieve it without them
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Recommendation 2: Design for Your Goal

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
### For Impact

**Prioritize accessibility**

The simplest path: ensure outputs are affordable and reachable

Or: build equitable partnerships
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### For Sustainability

**Choose your route**

Either: - Invest in quality + capacity, OR - Embed institutionally + extend timeline
:::
:::::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Recommendation 3: Make Equity Intentional

::: r-fit-text
**GESI focus is non-negotiable for equity outcomes**
:::

. . .

### The evidence is clear:

-   GESI appears in **100% of equity recipes**
-   **91%** of equity-achieving programmes had GESI focus (necessity)
-   GESI coverage is **93%** — it explains most equity success

. . .

::: callout-warning
## This means:

Equity cannot be an afterthought or a "nice to have." It must be integrated from design through implementation.
:::

## The Big Picture

::: callout-important
## Key Takeaway

**Different outcomes require different approaches**

There is no single "best practice" configuration that works for everything.
:::

| If you want...      | Focus on...                                  |
|---------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| Exceptional ratings | Prerequisites (necessary but not sufficient) |
| Impact              | Output accessibility (simplest path)         |
| Sustainability      | Quality delivery OR institutional embedding  |
| Equity              | Explicit GESI integration (mandatory)        |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Practical Implications {background-color="#f8f9fa"}

```{=html}
<div style="display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 0.8em; margin-top: 0.3em;">

<div style="background: #e8f5e9; padding: 0.6em; border-radius: 8px; border-left: 4px solid #388e3c;">
<div style="font-weight: bold; color: #388e3c; font-size: 0.8em; margin-bottom: 0.3em;">For Impact</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.6em; color: #333; line-height: 1.5;">
• <strong>Mandate open access** for all research outputs<br>
• Require <strong>plain-language summaries**<br>
• Design <strong>stakeholder-friendly formats** from the start<br>
<em style="color: #666;">This is the simplest, most powerful lever.</em>
</div>
</div>

<div style="background: #fff8e1; padding: 0.6em; border-radius: 8px; border-left: 4px solid #f57c00;">
<div style="font-weight: bold; color: #f57c00; font-size: 0.8em; margin-bottom: 0.3em;">For Equity</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.6em; color: #333; line-height: 1.5;">
• <strong>GESI is a design requirement**, not a reporting line<br>
• Build GESI into ToC, not just logframes<br>
• Accept that some "efficient" impact paths are off-limits<br>
<em style="color: #666;">This settles the "nice to have" debate.</em>
</div>
</div>

<div style="background: #fce4ec; padding: 0.6em; border-radius: 8px; border-left: 4px solid #c2185b;">
<div style="font-weight: bold; color: #c2185b; font-size: 0.8em; margin-bottom: 0.3em;">For Sustainability</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.6em; color: #333; line-height: 1.5;">
• <strong>Three routes:** outputs, ownership, or long-term funding<br>
• If outputs: invest in both accessible AND capacity<br>
• If ownership: governance + local embedding + multi-year<br>
<em style="color: #666;">FundingLongevity appears in 2 of 3 pathways.</em>
</div>
</div>

<div style="background: #e3f2fd; padding: 0.6em; border-radius: 8px; border-left: 4px solid #1976d2;">
<div style="font-weight: bold; color: #1976d2; font-size: 0.8em; margin-bottom: 0.3em;">For Programme Design</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.6em; color: #333; line-height: 1.5;">
• <strong>Be explicit about priority outcomes**<br>
• Don't assume all outcomes can be maximized<br>
• Potential trade-offs exist (e.g., ~GESI in one impact path)<br>
<em style="color: #666;">Honest priority-setting beats false promises.</em>
</div>
</div>

</div>
```
